pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria THE SMOKING GUN: Urine turning a dark port-wine color upon light exposure, accompanied by severe abdominal pain without surgical CT findings, dysautonomia, hyponatremia, and acute motor neuropathy precipitated by fasting. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant disorder resulting from a deficiency in hydroxymethylbilane synthase (porphobilinogen deaminase). Caloric restriction upregulates hepatic ALAS1, causing a surge in neurotoxic heme precursors, specifically delta-aminolevulinic acid and porphobilinogen. These toxic precursors cause acute autonomic, peripheral, and central nervous system dysfunction, manifesting as severe neuropathic abdominal pain, SIADH-induced hyponatremia, psychiatric distress, and motor paralysis. Exposure of excess porphobilinogen to light oxidizes it into porphobilin, turning the urine a classic port-wine color.
